questions.q: A user is a member of a role with GRANT SELECT on a table, but also has an explicit DENY SELECT on that same table. Can the user run a SELECT?
options: No — DENY always overrides a GRANT, regardless of where the GRANT came from
Yes — the most recently applied statement always wins
Yes — GRANT always overrides DENY for role-based access
It depends on whether the user is also a db_owner
questions.explain: DENY is the strongest permission statement in SQL Server — it overrides any GRANT on the same permission, from any source, including role membership.

options: Removes a previous GRANT or DENY statement, returning the permission to an unspecified state
Explicitly blocks a permission, the same as DENY
Grants full access to compensate for a removed restriction
Deletes the user account entirely from the database
questions.explain: REVOKE is not the same as DENY — it simply erases the previous permission statement rather than actively blocking access.

questions.q: Can db_owner role membership override an explicit DENY on a specific table for that same user?
options: No — an explicit DENY targeting that principal and object still overrides it
Yes — db_owner membership always overrides any DENY
Only if the DENY was applied before the db_owner grant
Only for DELETE permissions, not SELECT
questions.explain: DENY overrides GRANT regardless of the source of the GRANT, including powerful role memberships like db_owner.

questions.q: What does GRANT SELECT ON SCHEMA::dbo TO ReportingUser accomplish that granting SELECT on each individual table doesn't?
options: New tables added to the dbo schema later automatically inherit the grant
It grants SELECT only on tables that already existed at the time of the GRANT
It's functionally identical to granting SELECT at the server level
It only applies to views, not tables
questions.explain: A schema-level grant flows down to every object in that schema, present and future, which is more maintainable but broader in scope.

questions.q: What is the correct order of the SQL Server permission hierarchy, from broadest to most specific?
options: Server → Database → Schema → Object
Object → Schema → Database → Server
Database → Server → Object → Schema
Schema → Server → Database → Object
questions.explain: Permissions can be scoped at the server, database, schema, or object level, in that order from broadest to narrowest.
